thread:
incident-bot: :warning: DETECTED: Elevated DNS resolution errors for eu-west-1 endpoints (geo routing). Alerting oncall team.

liam_oncall: I'm on it. Confirming scope — are we seeing NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL from resolvers?

amira_neteng: Early checks show intermittent SERVFAIL from several EU recursive resolvers. US and APAC look fine. Could be Cloudflare GeoDNS or our Route53 healthchecks.

jess_ops: Customer reports: 'some EU users get 504s, others load fine' — seems like split-brain DNS. TTLs are 60s on geo records.

liam_oncall: Running `dig +trace` to eu endpoint from a few public resolvers. Sharing output: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example.eu A
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; SERVER: 1.1.1.1#53(1.1.1.1)
;; WHEN: Mon Mar 15 10:12:34 2026
```

patrick_sre: I can reproduce from an EU GCP instance: `dig` sometimes succeeds then fails. Looks like inconsistent answers from authoritative provider (Cloudflare).

cloudflare-status-bot: Cloudflare: We are investigating intermittent authoritative DNS failures in EU regions impacting geo steering for some customers — https://status.cloudflare.com/incident/xyz (internal).

liam_oncall: Ok that matches. Two tracks: 1) Mitigate traffic impact quickly for customers, 2) Engage provider support and prepare post-incident notes.

amira_neteng: Mitigation idea: temporarily set our geo fallback in Route53 to point EU traffic at the global LB IP (US region) so app remains reachable, then gradually fail traffic while we fix DNS. Need to lower risks around latency.

jess_ops: +1. Also notify customers that we're routing EU traffic to a fallback region to avoid downtime — CS and Support can post a notice.

liam_oncall: I'll flip GeoDNS failover to the fallback pool with a quick TTL bump. Steps: 
1) Increase TTL to 300 temporarily (to reduce churn) ??? Wait — we should reduce TTL to speed rollback. Setting TTL to 30 instead.
2) Update GeoDNS policy to route EU to fallback LB ip.
3) Monitor error rates and latency.

patrick_sre: Don't increase TTL. Keep low TTL (30) so we can revert quickly. Also enable additional healthcheck on fallback to prevent routing to unhealthy service.

liam_oncall: Performing the change now. Pasting CLI commands executed: 
```bash
# Route53 change-batch payload applied
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch file://change-eu-fallback.json
# change-eu-fallback.json routes geolocation EU to alias -> global-lb.example.com
```

liam_oncall: Change submitted. Change ID: C-ABCDEFG. Propagation should start immediately; TTL is 30s. Monitoring logs.

amira_neteng: I'm opening a support ticket with Cloudflare and attaching dig traces + packet captures. Ticket ID: CF-98765. Requesting immediate escalation to DNS engineering.

cloudflare-status-bot: Update: Cloudflare engineering investigating authoritative resolver failures in DE/IE regions. Intermittent SERVFAILs observed. ETA unknown.

jess_ops: Support and CS drafted customer message. Dalia, can you publish to the status page? Draft: "We're seeing intermittent DNS resolution issues for EU customers affecting access to API endpoints. We're routing affected traffic to a fallback region to restore availability; some requests may see increased latency. We're working with our DNS provider and will update here."

dalia_support: Publishing now to status.redwood.com (incident #INC-20260315-17). Also posting to onboarding customers flagged in last 30 days.

patrick_sre: Metrics: error budget alert still firing but RPS has stabilized after failover. 95th latency for EU jumped from 120ms -> 420ms. No sustained 5xxs from origin now.

liam_oncall: Good. Next: handoff plan. I'm on call for another 30m then Patrick takes over. Leaving runbook notes: 
- change-batch in Route53: C-ABCDEFG
- Cloudflare ticket CF-98765, assigned to oncall eng rep.
- rollback: apply original geo policy via change-eu-rollback.json and set TTL back to 60s.

patrick_sre: I'll take over. Will keep monitoring for DNS flapping and check if Cloudflare provides root cause. If we see requests to fallback > 50% for > 15m we should consider spinning up additional capacity in EU to reduce latency.

cloudflare-status-bot: Cloudflare update: Identified bug in geo steering cache invalidation affecting certain PoPs; mitigations applied to edge config. Propagation underway.

liam_oncall: Noted. If Cloudflare finishes remediation, we'll roll back geo failover. Patrick, coordinate rollback once we see stable successful authoritative answers for 10 minutes. Use this check: `dig @1.1.1.1 +short api.redwood.example.eu` should return EU-specific LB IP.

patrick_sre: Will do. Also capturing timeline for postmortem. Jess, please collect sample customer reports, and Amira, include packet captures and dig logs in the incident binder.

jess_ops: On it — collecting CS tickets and sample traces now.

cloudflare-status-bot: Update: Edge mitigation propagated. SERVFAIL rates decreasing. We'll post again when fully resolved.

patrick_sre: Seeing consistent successful answers from multiple EU resolvers now. 10min stable and latency trending down. Preparing rollback in 5m.

dalia_support: Customers notified of improved availability. Updating status page to reflect ongoing verification.

patrick_sre: Rolling back geo policy to original routing. Applied change-batch ID: C-HIJKLMN. TTL remains 30 for safety, will bump to 60 after 10m stable.

cloudflare-status-bot: Final: Issue mitigated. Root cause: cache invalidation bug in geo steering code path, fix deployed. Monitoring for regressions.

patrick_sre: Verified. EU resolvers returning expected geo answers, traffic shifted back. Latency back to ~140ms 95th. Marking incident as resolved, will file postmortem with timeline and remediation.

liam_oncall: Thanks team. Leaving notes in PagerDuty and incident binder. Handoff complete to Patrick.

patrick_sre: Closing thread — will attach postmortem draft in #postmortems in 48h. Thanks everyone for fast coordination. :tada:
